en.heading: 28 May: Flag Day opens a national display period until 12 June
en.origin: Flag Day begins on 28 May, commemorating the 1898 Battle of Alapan at Imus, Cavite, where the Philippine flag was raised during the struggle for independence. The historical episode is different from the date of a modern legal act. Proclamation No. 374 of 6 March 1965 declared 28 May of every year Flag Day, revoking an earlier 1949 proclamation. Its anniversary is not a single invention of flag symbolism. Republic Act No. 8491 of 1998 later specified that Flag Days span 28 May to 12 June and encourages government bodies, schools, businesses and homes to display the flag. This is a period with a clear opening day, not just a 24-hour celebration.

en.origin: The Philippine National Indigenous Peoples Day is held on 9 August to promote rights and the collective welfare of indigenous communities. Republic Act No. 10689, approved on 23 October 2015, established 9 August each year as a special working holiday and tasked the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples with implementation. The 9 August law is not the 29 October Indigenous Peoples Thanksgiving Day from 2003 nor the entire October Indigenous Peoples Month introduced in 2009. All three dates have different legal sources and should retain separate origin dossiers.
